title: bounded-optimizer-for-private-deployments: guarded commits & offline dry-runs
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Background: We want to surface automated batching/caching recommendations that reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs. For Private/VPC/on-prem customers we cannot assume telemetry egress or operator access patterns. This ticket implements a guarded optimizer workflow that produces recommendations, validates them against local policy, performs a signed dry-run (offline mode), and supports a controlled commit (guarded commit) with deterministic rollback. Scope: 1) generate constrained recommendations (batch limits, KV cache TTLs, prefix caching heuristics) suitable for private environments; 2) produce a self-contained dry-run plan file that can be reviewed/approved offline; 3) integrate a policy gate (OPA-based rules) and RBAC checks; 4) implement the guarded commit mechanism that uses a canary rollout across GPU pools and an automatic rollback on regression; 5) ensure audit logging and signed artifacts for compliance. Out of scope: model quantization changes that require image-level changes or hardware firmware updates.
acceptance_criteria: The optimizer can run in offline mode and emit a versioned JSON plan that contains diffs, estimated cost savings, and safety metadata.
Plans are validated by the local policy engine (configurable Rego rules) and rejected if they violate hard limits (max_batch_size, max_latency_p95 uplift, KV TTL drop below threshold).
Guarded commit implementation applies changes only to a single canary pool and monitors latency/cost metrics for an operator-configured window before promoting.
If monitored latency or error rate exceeds configured thresholds, the system automatically rolls back the canary and marks the plan as failed with an audit record.

All plan artifacts are signed with a customer key or Redwood signing key and stored alongside an immutable audit entry (for private setups, support local storage paths and optional S3-compatible endpoints).
Operators can perform a manual dry-apply on a single host with the same result as the automated commit (parity between CLI dry-run and platform apply).
tasks: Design offline plan schema (fields: plan_id, diffs, preflight_metrics, estimated_savings, safety_hints, signature)
Prototype local policy integration using OPA and provide example Rego rules for common private constraints
Implement plan signing and verification (support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM or local keypair)
Add canary rollout controller that applies plan to single GPU pool and integrates with console telemetry or local polling endpoints
Implement automatic rollback logic and deterministic revert plan generator
Add CLI commands: optimizer generate --offline, optimizer validate --policy <file>, optimizer commit --plan <file> --canary
Instrument audit events and local storage path support for private deployments
Write e2e tests covering offline generation -> validation -> canary apply -> rollback
notes: Trade-offs: stricter safe defaults reduce savings but are required for zero-trust private customers. Allowing per-customer policy loosens defaults but increases testing surface.
We will avoid automatic quantization toggles in Private mode unless customer explicitly opts in via an authenticated feature flag.
Telemetry constraints: where outbound metrics are blocked, use push-to-host or pull-from-agent patterns and allow operator-provided metric endpoints for monitoring canary.
Policy enforcement will be dual-mode: 'hard' rules that block apply and 'soft' rules that create warnings and require explicit operator override.
Consider using cryptographic signatures and simple GitOps-style plan objects so customers can store plans in their internal repos for review workflows.
comments: 2026-02-21 | PM review (R. Gupta): Make sure cost estimates in the plan include both token-cost and expected GPU-time impact (warm cache vs cold cache).
2026-02-25 | Design feedback (N. Alvarez): Provide a compact UI representation for offline plans in Console. For on-prem customers without console, provide CLI summary and an HTML report export.
2026-03-04 | Security (M. O'Neill): Require signed plans when security_review_required=true; recommend customers use their KMS to manage signing keys. We should add HSM/KMS integration stories.

2026-03-10 | Eng sync (L. Chen): Spike complete for plan schema and OPA prototype. Found edge case where batch size changes can increase tail latency for stateful models; added safety rule to cap batch growth to max(ceil(1.2 * historic_median_batch), absolute_max).
2026-03-13 | QA (S. Park): Added test matrix for environments with no outbound telemetry — validated that CLI-driven canary monitoring returns correct failure signals when simulated latency rises.
decision_log: Use OPA (Rego) for local policy enforcement to allow customers to author constraints without changing platform code.
Plan artifacts will be JSON with a canonical schema and signed; signature verification will run before any commit in private deployments.
Guarded commits will default to a 1-pool canary for 30 minutes with configurable thresholds; customers can shorten or lengthen the window.
Avoid any mandatory outbound data collection; where necessary, provide a secure push-to-redwood option that customers can opt into.
Do not include model-weight-level changes in automated optimizer for private until we have validated rollback reliability across hardware variants.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement schema, OPA integration, CLI dry-run and unit tests
Phase 1 (internal beta): enable on a subset of internal dedicated accounts with synthetic workloads; validate metrics and rollback
Phase 2 (customer pilot): invite two private customers with different constraints (air-gapped and VPC-hosted) to pilot and collect feedback
Phase 3 (general availability): enable via Console and CLI for private deployments with documentation and default Rego rules
rollback_plan: Every plan includes a deterministic revert payload that can be applied immediately to restore previous batching/caching config
Automated rollback trigger: p95 latency increase > 20% OR error rate increase > 1% above baseline during canary window
Manual rollback: operators can run 'optimizer rollback --plan <plan_id> --force' which verifies signature and applies revert payload
Post-rollback: create an incident ticket and attach plan, audit log, and monitoring traces for RCA
